speaker: Doctor
text: You have jaundice, pruritus, weight loss, pale stool, and dark urine, which strongly suggests obstructive jaundice. To narrow down the cause, do you have any history of gallstones or recent abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 72-year-old male. The patient has experienced gradual yellow discoloration of the skin and generalized pruritus over the past 2 weeks. He also reports a decreased appetite and a weight loss of 6.3 kg (14 lb). The patient’s stool has been pale, and his urine is very dark. Three years ago, he had an episode of acute upper abdominal pain, which was managed with IV fluids, NSAIDs, and dietary modification. speaker: Doctor
text: Given your age, significant weight loss, and painless jaundice, I am concerned about a malignancy such as pancreatic cancer. I will order imaging to visualize the biliary tree and pancreas. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal CT Scan

speaker: Doctor
text: A normal CT scan is unusual for pancreatic cancer, so I need to look closer at the bile ducts. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the imaging is normal, I suspect an inflammatory condition like Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis rather than a structural obstruction. REQUEST TEST: Liver Function Tests

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin_Total: 5.6 mg/dL, Direct_Bilirubin: 4.8 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase: 192 U/L, AST: 32 U/L, ALT: 34 U/L

speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results confirm a cholestatic pattern with elevated direct bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase, but the normal imaging makes large duct obstruction unlikely. To investigate a micro-abscholic cause, do you have a history of inflammatory bowel disease, particularly ulcerative colitis?

speaker: Patient
text: has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 years. He has a 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the cholestatic pattern and normal imaging, I suspect Primary Biliary Cholangitis, especially given your age and gender profile, though it is less common in men. REQUEST TEST: Anti-Mitochondrial Antibodies

speaker: Doctor
text: With negative AMA and normal imaging, Primary Biliary Cholangitis is unlikely, so I suspect Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis or IgG4-related disease. REQUEST TEST: IgG4 levels

speaker: Doctor
text: Since IgG4 and AMA are normal, I need to rule out autoimmune hepatitis or other inflammatory causes. REQUEST TEST: Antinuclear Antibodies

speaker: Doctor
text: With negative autoimmune markers and normal imaging, I suspect a medication-induced cholestasis or a rare infiltrative disease. Are you currently taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter supplements, or herbal remedies?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Episode of acute upper abdominal pain treated three years ago. History of long-term alcohol consumption and smoking. Social history: Stopped alcohol consumption three years ago; 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.

speaker: Doctor
text: You have painless jaundice, weight loss, and cholestatic labs with normal structural imaging, which strongly points to an infiltrative process like lymphoma or metastatic disease that hasn't formed a mass yet. DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma
